## Status: the cut-over is done

Stencil moved ACH origination and return processing off Rails/Sidekiq onto the Go `ach-originator`
service per ADR-024, after the April 6 P0 where Sidekiq stalled and Pillar Bank's 6 PM PT cutoff was missed for 2,138 auto-deposits

($147k) [c2][c16].

- The target was end of June, but the **June 27 load test failed at 3x** on outbox vacuum contention.

After fixes, July runs passed at 3x and 4x [c7][c16].
- Shadow mode ran **Aug 4–17** with only 3 early diffs, all fixed.

The Aug 14 go/no-go returned conditional GO, and a one-flag Sidekiq rollback was tested Aug 12 [c8][c15].
- **Primary on

Aug 18**, with **zero missed cutoffs since** [c7][c15].
- The **30-day rollback hold ended Sep 17**, and the September Pillar

MBR approved deleting the legacy Sidekiq ACH code [c1][c7].
- Sarah Kim became secondary pipeline owner and, as of **Oct

2**, owns the weekly Pillar ops sync, with Marcus as escalation only [c16][c25].

The **Sep 26 SEV1 duplicate round-up debit**
(1,412 users, $12,708) did *not* involve the Go pipeline. It was the legacy Rails/Sidekiq round-up sweep, which lacked an

idempotency key [c3][c10]. It still drives most of what's open with Pillar.

## What's still open

**Due or overdue** (Oct

2 Pillar Ops Sync) [c25]:

| Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|
| Tune NACHA-cutoff alert | Marcus | Oct 13 |
| Deletion

notice to Theresa's team | Devon | Oct 13 |
| **Delete Sidekiq ACH code** | Devon | Oct 16 |
| Remediation plan to Theresa

Lowe + Priya Shah | Maya | Oct 15 |
| Shared open-items list | Sarah | Oct 9 *(past due; no completion shown)* |

**Sidekiq
ACH deletion** was approved Sep 17 but hadn't happened by the Oct 7 1on1. Devon was on the reconciliation fix, and the decision
was deletion right after, **no later than Oct 16**. The rationale: "dead money-moving code that anyone can re-enable with
a config change is how we got Sep 26 on a different job" [c24]. It's tracked as an open risk, though via an *inferred* edge

[c5].

**NACHA-cutoff alert** noise traces to the April 6 postmortem. The risk is that noise trains people to ignore the

one alert that exists because of April 6 [c7][c16][c25].

**Pillar remediation:** Pillar wants a plan by **Oct 15** proving
idempotency across all eleven money-moving jobs. An inventory found **seven of eleven non-idempotent** and one partial [c11][c13].

Two ADRs carry it:
- **ADR-031** (Proposed): sha256 idempotency keys in a unique-indexed `money_movement_keys` table, enforced

via a `MoneyMoving` concern and RuboCop cop. **Due Oct 23** [c13][c14].
- **ADR-032**: the Q4 migration of the round-up

sweep and other legacy jobs onto the ADR-024 outbox pipeline, also a dependency for card round-ups [c13][c14].

**Smaller

follow-ups:** dashboard lag, and load concentrated on Marcus, with the Sarah handoff as mitigation [c16][c18].

**Risk to
flag:** Devon is also on the position-reconciliation fix (review Oct 14, go/no-go #2 Oct 16). The manager note says he can't
do both well in one month [c24], so the Oct 16 deletion could slip.

data.text:
# The April 6 ACH Outage: Decisions and Follow-Up Status

## What happened

On Sunday April 6, Sidekiq workers stalled during
the ACH batch and NACHA file generation hung on a rarely used O(n²) serialization path, triggered by 800+ entries, 35% of
them modified-ACH. Retries amplified the stall, and the batch missed Pillar Bank's 6 PM PT cutoff. **2,138 auto-deposits

totaling $147k were delayed three business days.** No funds were lost [c2][c8][c26].

## What you decided

- **Architecture:**
ADR-024, "Move ACH Processing Off Sidekiq." The monolith writes to an `ach_outbox` table, a Go relay publishes to `ach-intents.fifo`

SQS, a leader-elected `ach-originator` builds and submits files, and a separate ingester handles returns [c2][c23].
- **Policy:**
a codified $25 credit for any delay caused by your error, a Sunday on-call update, and a missed-cutoff protocol with Pillar

Bank [c8].
- **Lessons:** test or remove money-movement paths; known fragility compounds; monitoring is not detection; comms

speed beats polish [c8][c12].

## Follow-ups: eight of nine closed

The hotfix, batch-size alerts, compensation policy,
ADR-024, Sunday on-call update, 3x load test, customer-comms runbook, and Pillar missed-cutoff protocol are all done [c8].
The rebuild landed late: the first Sunday load test on June 27 failed at 3x, pushing cut-over to August. Shadow mode ran

Aug 4–17, cut-over was Aug 18, and there have been **zero missed cutoffs since** [c8][c9][c19].

## Two items still open,

both due within days

**1. NACHA-cutoff alert tuning (Marcus, due Oct 13).** This is the last original action item, and
it has slipped. The alert also fires too often on normal Sunday volume. Your note: *"An alert people learn to ignore is

the April 6 failure mode again"* [c8][c32]. It's also an open commitment in your Oct 1 1:1 with Marcus [c22].

**2. Sidekiq
ACH code deletion (Devon, due Oct 16).** This is a downstream item from the rebuild, not on the original list. The 30-day
stability hold ended Sep 17 and the September Pillar MBR approved deletion [c8][c16][c28]. Devon has been on the fractional-share
reconciliation fix, which you agreed was the right priority. Your Oct 7 decision: **recon fix first, deletion right after,

no later than Oct 16** [c29][c31]. Devon also owes Theresa's team a written deletion notice by Oct 13 [c32].

Your reason
for urgency: dead money-moving code that can be re-enabled by a config change is how Sep 26 happened on a different job.

It's tracked as an open risk owned by Devon [c3][c29].

## Assessment

The structural fix shipped and the pipeline has held
clean since August. But the two open items are detection and hygiene, which map to your own lessons #3 and #1 [c8][c12].
Marcus, who owns the alert tuning, is flagged in your 1:1 notes as a burnout risk, which may explain the slippage [c22][c17].

data.text:
## Where SOC 2 Type II stands

**Type I is done and clean.** Ledgerwise Assurance issued an unqualified SOC 2 Type I report
on 2026-06-30, covering control design as of 2026-05-31 against Security and Availability, with 2 observations [c8][c6].
Those observations have since been closed [c12]. The report is internal-only; sharing requires an NDA and Maya Chen's approval

[c8].

**The Type II window is open, 2026-07-01 to 2026-12-31** [c8][c7]. Type II tests whether controls *operated* across
the whole window, not just that they were designed correctly [c8]. Sam Whitfield owns the program, Maya Chen is executive

approver [c1].

Scope: production AWS, the Rails monolith, Go money movement services, mobile backend APIs, CI/CD and tooling.
Snowflake analytics and the marketing site are out. AWS, Pillar Bank, Plaid, Alloy and DriveWealth are carved-out subservice

organizations [c1][c8].

## The gaps

Sam's 2026-09-10 midpoint readiness review found **three gaps that would produce Type

II exceptions if not closed and documented** [c18]. Status is as of the Oct 9 update, so possibly ~2 days stale:

| # |

Gap | Severity | Due | Status (Oct 9) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Q3 quarterly access review not done | High | 2026-10-10

| 70% (14 of 20 systems) |
| 2 | Vendor risk assessments missing: DriveWealth, Lithic, Alloy, Customer.io | Medium | 2026-10-24

| 2 of 4 done |
| 3 | MDM on 88% of laptops; control requires 100% | Medium | 2026-10-17 | 96% (65 of 68) |

All three are

owned by Sam.

**Gap 1: access review.** Q3 hadn't started by Sep 10, largely because Sam spent August on policies and owners
were busy with the ACH cut-over and investing beta. The Sep 21–30 rerun **missed Sep 30** [c18]. Six systems remain: Plaid
and Lithic dashboards (Tier 1, Marcus), PagerDuty and Snowflake (Tier 2), Customer.io and Branch (Tier 3) [c22]. Two are
Tier 1 money-moving vendor portals, a harder story than "lower-risk tools." The late completion will be documented as an

exception with root cause, and **Q4's review starts Dec 1** to avoid a repeat [c18].

**Gap 2: vendor assessments.** DriveWealth
closed 2026-09-24 and Lithic 2026-10-02. **Still open: Alloy (waiting on their SOC 2 bridge letter) and Customer.io (questionnaire
with their team)** [c18]. Both depend on outside parties, so Oct 24 isn't fully in Sam's control. Policy requires assessment

before contract and annual review for any vendor touching Confidential or Restricted data [c11][c10].

**Gap 3: MDM.** Of
68 laptops, enrollment went 11 (Jul 31) → 39 (Aug 21) → 60 (Sep 10) → 65 (Oct 8) [c20]. **Three remain**: two Linux workstations
(endpoint agent plus script-enforced baseline; one installed, second scheduled Oct 13) and one laptop of someone on leave
until Oct 14, enrolled on return and blocked from SSO meanwhile [c18][c20]. No exceptions were granted. Phase 5 (posture

check blocks SSO) waits for 100% [c20].

## Other open threads

- **Investing scope is unconfirmed.** Sam still needs to

confirm it with Ledgerwise [c1][c14]; late scoping means evidence for a period already partly elapsed.
- **Exceptions register

unpublished.** Sam has an open action to publish it [c9], relevant since Gap 1 will be an exception.
- **Northfield diligence.**

Maya owns sending the status letter and data room, with a call on Oct 14 [c1][c14][c12].

## Framing

All three gaps are
remediation in progress, not unknowns. But closing a gap in October doesn't erase the months it was open, so Gap 1 is already
a certain exception and the goal is documenting it well. Closing these before the window ends was a Q4 priority that helped

push the card soft launch from Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 [c2][c24].

Caveat: figures trace to the Oct 9 update and Oct 8 MDM snapshot.
Today is Oct 11 and Gap 1's target was Oct 10, so it may already have closed; nothing more recent shows up.

"GA target Oct 20, **at risk**" is the standing language across the launch map, product
teamspace, and Oct 9 status rollup [c13][c10][c3]. Go/no-go #2 on **Friday Oct 16** decides GA for **Tuesday Oct 20** [c9][c30].

Go/no-go #1 on Sep 29 was a NO-GO [c13][c12].

## The blockers and their owners

Three blockers came out of go/no-go #1.

One is closed, two are open [c15][c30]:

| # | Blocker | Owner | Status (Oct 9) | Due |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Position

reconciliation fix | **Devon Park** | In code review; rollout plan being written | Oct 14 |
| B2 | Disclosures final review

| **Hana Ito** | Signed Oct 7, **cleared** | Done |
| B3 | Android parity (2 screens) | **Nadia Okafor** | Order confirmation

done; performance detail in progress | Oct 15 |

**B1 is the hard gate.** 0.4% of investing positions are off by fractional
shares against DriveWealth, all tracing to a stock split in an underlying ETF holding: Stencil's ledger applies the split
ratio and rounds, while DriveWealth carries more precision [c16]. Positions that don't reconcile block GA outright; "everything
else is negotiable" [c13]. The PR is verified against all 46 affected positions but still needs a re-run with 0 mismatches

[c7][c8].

**B3** is UI-only work, since business rules live in `brokerd`. Open items are the flag-gated merge, design QA,

disclosure verification, and Play Store submission. Android performance remains a concern [c28][c29].

## What is most likely

to break the date

GO requires **100% of positions reconciled on two consecutive daily runs after the fix** [c30]. If the
fix lands Oct 14, there is no slack. The agenda says it plainly: "The fix lands late on Oct 14 and the Oct 15 run is our

only clean day. Then we either accept one day or slip" [c30]. Devon owns this GA-slip risk [c29][c11].

Other GO criteria:
B1/B3 closed with evidence, no open SEV1/SEV2 touching money movement, and no compliance objection from Hana, who holds

a **veto**. Renee chairs, with Maya Chen and Aleks Varga as decision makers [c30][c9].

## Second-order risks

- The board

meeting is **Oct 21**, the day after target GA, and a second NO-GO would land in the Oct 16 pre-read [c1][c30].
- Kavi wants
a 25% ramp on Oct 20; Maya prefers waiting until after the board. The plan is 25% → 50% Oct 22 → 100% Oct 26, each step

gated on clean reconciliation [c30][c29].
- A GA slip is a named **Series B closing risk**, and investing readiness is a

probable diligence question [c2].
- "20x DriveWealth load untested" is also flagged, owned by Devon [c3]. iOS-only GA is

an open question with no decision recorded [c29].

- Devon: reconciliation fix by **Oct 14** [c30]

- Nadia: Android parity by **Oct 15** [c30]
- Renee: refreshed checklist and pre-read by **Oct 15** [c30]
- Kavi: ramp plan

## Risks others have raised that still sit open on you

**1. Marcus's burnout: acknowledged,

not resolved.**
On Aug 26 he told you plainly he's tired: ACH cut-over, KYC migration, the Pillar sync, interviews, and
on-call backstop since April, with no full week off since February [c38]. You committed him to a full week off in September;
he took three days [c41]. Your note after the Sep 26 postmortem says he handed the Pillar sync to Sarah and "did not seem
fine" [c17]. The risk appears in at least four places, all still open [c35][c39][c37]. The structural cause is that Marcus
is manager, TL and on-call backstop for Payments at once [c39]. Your mitigation, the VP Eng hire, is months away. His concrete
ask also looks unactioned: shadow-diff review should be a rotation from day one, not his personal sign-off every morning

[c38].

**2. Nadia's comp: raised twice, and she doesn't believe you.**
On Sep 15 she said she's been a TL and manager since
Aug 18, paid as a TL, and that this was the second time she'd heard "post-Series B" [c51]. Your note: "if I miss this, I
lose more than money with her" [c51]. On Oct 6 she replied "I'll believe it when it's on paper" [c49]. Two commitments are
unchecked: the senior iOS band with Jordan (due Oct 23) and Nadia's comp review after close (due Nov 30) [c49]. The band

problem is structural: every senior iOS decline this year cited comp [c42].

**3. Ama's offer: above band, comp approval

was due Oct 10.**
Her ask is above the current band, and approval was needed by Oct 10, which has passed [c53]. The risk

of losing Ama and restarting the search is still open [c1].

**4. Devon's staff case.**
He told you in May he was getting
recruiter outreach and wanted to grow [c58], and asked in September what a staff case looks like [c54]. Your commitment
to write it down with Marcus by Oct 23 is unchecked [c54][c59]. Your Oct 7 read: "the comp still has to land after close,

though" [c59]. The Payments understaffing risk is still open and owned by you [c58].

**5. Lin.**
You volunteered that she's

underpaid and promised an adjustment after the Series B [c50]. She's the sole designer.

**6. Sam's SOC 2 access review.**
The risk is a Type II exception [c1][c37]. It was 70% complete in the letter draft [c13] and 55% at Eng Staff on Oct 5 [c53].
Your note: "if Q3 access review isn't done by 10/10, this letter gets less true every day it sits there" [c23]. The data

room upload is due Oct 12, tomorrow.

**7. Devon's GA blockers.**
Fractional-share drift: 0.4% of positions are off against
DriveWealth in a beta with real money [c57]. 20x DriveWealth load is untested [c2]. Dormant ACH code can still be re-enabled

by config [c18], with deletion pending to Oct 16 [c54][c60].

**8. Structural and ownerless risks.**
"Decision bottleneck"
and "what is engineering optimizing for during Series B?" are open on your own notes [c4]. You and Marcus carry nearly every
money-movement, fundraising and hiring thread [c17], and four deadlines between 10/12 and 10/17 route through you [c2].

"Android team falling behind" and "card economics weakened by interchange compression" have no owner [c4].

**9. Two undecided

calls.**
Whether to tell Grace Liu about the Sep 26 incident before or after reference checks (leaning before) [c14], and

whether to name the auditor's expected exception in the SOC 2 letter (leaning yes) [c23].

---

**The pattern worth naming:**
Nadia, Devon and Lin each hold a comp promise that resolves at the same post-close moment, and one already told you she
won't believe it until it's on paper. That's a correlated retention risk, and nothing in the map shows it being managed

as one thing.

A caveat: several groupings above are marked `inferred` in the graph rather than drawn directly from a note,
so treat them as derived [c18][c27][c1].

data.text:
## The state of play

Your decision matrix already has a narrow verdict. Weights were locked Sep 30, before either final
round, so you couldn't reverse-engineer them to fit a favorite [c29]. Weighted scores as of Oct 9: **Grace 4.0, Tomas 3.65**

[c29].

- Grace wins C1 hiring engine (25%: 5 vs 3), C4 culture fit (5 vs 2), C5 manager development (5 vs 3) and C6 TL

panel confidence (5 vs 3) [c29].
- Tomas wins C2 regulated money movement (20%: 5 vs 2) and C3 ops load off Marcus/Maya

(20%: 5 vs 3) [c29].

Both came through Hollis Partners; Grace's final round was Oct 6, Tomas's Oct 8 [c41][c40].

## The

case for Grace Liu

**She wins the heaviest criterion.** She's a director of engineering at a large consumer neobank (ex-Chime),
running ~60 engineers and having grown the org from 22 to 60 in two and a half years. Her offer-accept rate is ~80% [c41],
against your current 55%, where every senior iOS decline named comp [c2]. You need 12 hires in 9 months [c29][c3]; that

gap is the whole ballgame.

**The loop liked her.** Her case study was the best of the search: customer impact first, "stop
the bleeding" separated from "fix the class of problem," a launch slip of a sprint, and a question about who on the team
was carrying the most [c41][c8][c14]. Aleks: "I'd work with her. She'd tell me no." The TL panel gave two strong hires and
one hire [c41]. She has coached two first-time managers, which is what Nadia needs [c41][c29]. Your own framing: "the real

fix for Marcus is a team, not a manager who knows NACHA. She builds the team faster" [c29].

**What's holding her back:**
She has never run a regulated money-movement org [c41]. Marcus: "she'll need to learn NACHA and Pillar from us, and we're
the ones who are tired" [c41]. Her current org is twice your size, and her package is above your proposed band, though Hollis
thinks she'd move for equity and scope [c41]. Open questions: can she take the Pillar ops relationship off Marcus in 90

days, and who does she go to when Maya and Marcus disagree? [c41]

## The case for Tomas Reyes

**He owns the 40% of weight
that hurts today.** He scores 5 and 5 on C2 and C3 [c29]. Your summary: "the case for Tomas is 'Marcus gets relief in month
one'" [c29]. Ex-Brex, he's run money movement at scale and handled sponsor-bank relationships and incident command, which
is "exactly the experience Grace doesn't have" [c40]. That matters after two money-movement incidents this year [c29] and
the Sep 26 duplicate round-up debit [c1][c17]. Elena Sorensen "would like him on paper," relevant to the Oct 14 diligence

list [c40][c25].

**What's holding him back:** He's very process-heavy. He spent ~10 minutes on his RACI template and decision-review
cadence: "Thorough. Also the moment I started worrying." You think Marcus and Devon would read it as distrust and "comply
and quietly disengage" [c40]. That echoes the "process maximalist" anti-pattern in your search brief, flagged at severity
70, the highest risk on the hiring plan [c23][c3]. Nadia gave a no-hire, and he's weaker on growing managers [c25][c40].
**Your sharpest self-check:** *"part of me wants Tomas because he'd make the regulated side feel safe, and that's my fear
talking, not my judgment. The other part notices he never once asked who on the team was tired"* [c40], which is the question

Grace did ask [c41].

## What's still open before Oct 20

The decision is due Oct 20, the day before the board meeting [c1][c29].

- Grace's references due Oct 13; the **peer director, payments** is the one that matters for money movement [c41]
- Back-channel

call via Dana Whitaker by Oct 14 [c41]
- Grace's money-movement 30/60/90 sketch due Oct 12 [c41]
- 1:1 with each TL by Oct

15 [c29]
- **Tomas's references haven't started**; open question whether to run them in parallel at ~a week of recruiter

time [c25]

C2 and C4 are the scores most likely to move [c29], and a 0.35-point spread is thin enough that they're decisive.
**Framing:** the matrix says Grace, with dissent concentrated in one known gap and a named mitigation path. The link between
the "process maximalist" risk and Tomas is my own; your notes flag them separately [c23][c40].
